beats.text: Two friends are checking numbered tickets for a school event. Almost every digit matches! Which ticket comes first? A quick glance at the final digits could fool us, so let’s investigate from the right starting place.
Today, we’re learning to compare and order whole numbers using place value.

beats.text: Which number is larger when most of the digits match? Compare from the greatest place value, not from the right. For whole numbers with no leading zeros, more digits means a larger number. If the lengths match, compare one column at a time.
Which ticket number is greater? Point to the first place where the digits differ. We can stop once we find it.

Compare four hundred and fifty six thousand, seven hundred and eighty two, with four hundred and fifty six thousand, seven hundred and twenty eight. Their hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands and hundreds match. We have not found a difference yet, so keep moving right.

At the tens place, eight is greater than two. Stop there. The first number is greater, so four hundred and fifty six thousand, seven hundred and eighty two is greater than four hundred and fifty six thousand, seven hundred and twenty eight. The ones cannot overturn that difference.
Try this pair before I show the comparison. Will the many nines at the end decide the answer, or will an earlier place decide?

Now compare three hundred and nine thousand, nine hundred and fifty, with three hundred and ten thousand and five. The hundred thousands match. At ten thousands, zero is less than one. Therefore three hundred and nine thousand, nine hundred and fifty is smaller.

To order several numbers, repeat the same method. Eighty nine thousand, nine hundred and ninety nine comes before ninety thousand and one, which comes before ninety thousand and ten. Do not compare only the final three digits. The greatest differing place decides.
board: Start left; stop at the first difference

beats.text: Sam compares only the final three digits and thinks eighty-nine thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine must be greater than ninety thousand and one. That overlooks the ten-thousands! Nine ten-thousands is greater than eight ten-thousands, whatever follows.
board: Start left, not at the final digits.

beats.text: The first differing place is the tens. Three tens is greater than zero tens, so 582,430 is greater.

As a supporting estimation check, rounding eighty nine thousand, nine hundred and ninety nine to the nearest thousand gives ninety thousand. A rounded value is useful, but it does not replace an exact comparison. Recap: line up the places, start left, find the first difference, and explain your order.
board: Line up → start left → first difference

beats.chapter: Look what you can do now
beats.text: Our goal was to compare and order whole numbers using place value. You can now explain your strategy, check the places carefully, and show why your answer makes sense. Choose a number of your own and explain it to someone nearby.
